en: One fascicle of the Ritual for the Offering and Recitation for Attaining Accomplishment of the Bodhisattva Amṛtakuṇḍalī.
Compiled by the Grand Master of State Ceremonial, Special Advancement, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, Duke of Sui.
I take refuge in Vajrapāṇi, the Great Bodhisattva and Lord of Secrets,
who can expound the Supreme Vehicle; who causes one to swiftly realize the nectar of enlightenment,
and who is able to destroy all demonic obstacles— Amṛtakuṇḍalī.
Through the skillful means of compassionate wisdom, he manifests as a great wrathful form,
a great and majestic sun-disk; by illuminating the darkness of the infinite realms of practitioners,
he causes them to swiftly attain siddhi.
Flowing with the water of ambrosia, it washes away the various seeds of habitual tendencies within the *ālayavijñāna*;
swiftly gathering the accumulations of merit and wisdom, one attains the perfectly pure *dharmakāya*.
Therefore, I prostrate with my head bowed in reverence.
Now, relying upon the secret mantras, I shall explain the nectar-like ritual manual according to the teachings on the subtle principles; first,
the ācārya should select a disciple for the practice of secret mantras who possesses pure faith in the Triple Gem.
Loving and honoring the Mahāyāna, thirsting for and admiring the teachings of Yoga,
they delight in practicing the bodhisattva conduct;
their minds are not timid or weak as they seek to study the gateway of correspondence, relinquishing body, life, and wealth.
Free from weariness and stinginess, born of noble lineage and endowed with all faculties,
they are learned and protect the True Dharma; delighting in the practice of the six perfections,
they compassionately regard all sentient beings and are ever clad in the great armor of their vows.
To fully deliver all classes of sentient beings throughout boundless realms and cause them to swiftly realize bodhi—
if an ācārya perceives such a person who is a vessel for the Dharma, he shall skillfully exhort and guide them.
First, one should expound for them the subtle path of the bodhisattva,
the skillful principles of prajñā, and the swift road to enlightenment;
then, having conferred the three refuges, cause them to generate the bodhicitta.
Next, having conferred the three types of unimpeded bodhisattva vows pertaining to the three times,
one should then lead [the disciple] into the maṇḍala and confer the vidyādhara initiations of their respective tutelary deities.
One should show the maṇḍala and proclaim the samaya:
"From now until the attainment of Buddhahood, do not abandon the bodhicitta;
revere the ācārya as equal to all Buddhas."
Just like Vajrapāṇi, one should maintain deep respect for one's fellow practitioners and never treat them with contempt;
having received the vajra and the vajra-ghaṇṭā from the teacher,
one does so for the sake of attaining siddhi.
Until reaching the site of enlightenment, one should never abandon the face-to-face empowerment master;
having fully received the instructions of the tutelary deity with certainty and without error,
one should thereafter practice with courageous diligence.
The practitioner of yoga,
having received the ritual manual of the deity from the master,
should dwell in a secluded place, such as a mountain forest or a deep valley.
In a superior location as described in various teachings,
one should establish a pure chamber,
whether in a vihāra or within a stūpa.
Purify the ground by smearing it with cow dung and apply white sandalwood paste to the maṇḍala,
making it either square or circular according to one's preference and size.
Scatter various kinds of flowers upon the altar.
Arrange and adorn it with ointment, incense, food offerings, lamps,
and argha water, as far as your means allow.
One should install the image of the principal deity within the chamber facing west,
while the practitioner faces east.
Prostrating with the entire body cast upon the ground, one offers oneself;
the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas accept one as their sovereign.
The mantra says:
Oṃ sarvatathāgatapūjā-pratīcchana-samaye namo niryātayāmi sarvatathāgataśāśvatadharmatāṃ sarvatathāgatānām avisaṃvādakaḥ. Reciting this secret mantra, one should form this reflection:
In the great ocean-like assemblies of all Buddhas throughout the dust-mote lands of all worlds in the ten directions,
there is one's own body in each;
before every member of the holy assembly, one offers up one's body in service.
Through the empowerment of the mantra,
one receives the protection and acceptance of all the noble hosts.
Furthermore, one should prostrate with the five limbs touching the ground.
Again, one should visualize oneself prostrating at the feet of all Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas.
The mantra is: Oṃ sarvatathāgatapādavandanāṃ karomi. By the empowerment of this mantra, [the prostration is accomplished].
It enables the practitioner,
without rising from their seat, to reach everywhere throughout the ten directions and to truly pay homage to all the Buddhas,
Tathāgatas, within the ocean-like assemblies of every atom and land.
Next, one should place the right knee on the ground,
join the palms at the heart, close the eyes,
and direct the mind to contemplate throughout the void the infinite and boundless oceans of assemblies of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas within the dust-motes of all lands.
The assembly descends to the place of the yogin. Furthermore,
one visualizes oneself before each of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas,
holding various types of ointments, powdered incense, flower garlands, burning incense, divine and exquisite food and drink, lamps, and precious torches.
I dedicate this to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Without rising from this seat,
may I compassionately regard the entire realm of sentient beings without exception who drift through the six realms of existence.
Due to the false conceptualization of one's own mind,
one becomes deluded regarding the ultimate truth and commits various unwholesome deeds,

thereby inviting the ripening of diverse fruits of suffering. Observing the realms of humans and devas, one encounters the suffering of not obtaining what one seeks through attachment to the five sensual pleasures.
In the celestial realms, they manifest the suffering of transformation;
with the blossoming of the flower of sublime awakening,
they open their bodhicitta and contemplate the cold hells.
By burning fragrant incense,
they are freed from the sufferings of cold and ice within the realm of hungry ghosts.
By means of this food and drink, divinely and wondrously empowered,
may they be fully satisfied and free from the karma of stinginess.
He contemplates the realms of asuras, animals, and the form and formless realms,
where beings with minds characterized by deceit, guile, and anger mutually inflict harm upon one another,
and those who are addicted to the flavor of meditative absorption.
By means of this Lamp of My Prajñā,
may all their entanglements of delusion be entirely removed,
so that they may stand before the ocean-like assembly of Buddhas.
With devotion, one confesses the obscurations of the three times;
one rejoices in all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, and Pratyekabuddhas,
and rejoices in the accumulations of merit and wisdom throughout the three times.
Then one contemplates all classes of sentient beings within the infinite and boundless realms of the defiled world,
all of whom have realized unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Furthermore, one visualizes oneself before each and every one of those Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
"Please turn the unsurpassed wheel of Dharma;
remain long in this world and do not enter nirvana.
Then the yogin sat down cross-legged.
Alternatively, one may sit as one pleases in the half-lotus posture.
A practitioner of yoga should not cling to external purity;
rather, they should always [bathe] with the water of the dharmas that are naturally pure in the ultimate sense.
Purify the body and mind in accordance with the principle of reality.
Recite the mantra of purification three times:
Oṃ svabhāva-śuddhāḥ sarvadharmāḥ svabhāva-śuddho ’haṃ. As it is taught in the *Vajraśekhara-yoga-sūtra*.
With the vajras of body, speech, and mind, taking the bodhicitta as the foremost,
and with a pure mind as one's bath, the practitioner of benefit and bliss should take the fragrant ointment and smear it upon both hands.
Place the palms together at the heart and immediately form the samaya-mudrā of the Tathāgata family,
like palms joined as if holding an unfurled lotus.
One should attach the *vīrya* (effort) finger to the upper joint of the *kṣānti* (patience) finger,
and attach the *dhyāna* (meditation) and *prajñā* (wisdom) fingers respectively to the sides of the *vīrya* finger.
Having thus formed the mudrā, one recites the mantra.
Entering into yogic mental attention (*manasikāra*),
one contemplates that all Tathāgatas pervade space and grant their empowerment through their vows.
I further imagine that immeasurable rays of light stream forth from the mudrā.
Illuminating and touching all sentient beings without exception,
may they swiftly realize the equality of true suchness (tathatā) by means of this Buddha-samaya-mudrā.
May I swiftly realize yoga.
May all sentient beings attain ultimate, great enlightenment.
The mantra is as follows:
Namo samanta-buddhānām. Oṃ tathāgata-nābhiya svāhā. By reciting this while forming the mudrā and focusing the mind, [the rite is accomplished].
One will become equal to the Tathāgata and obtain the thirty-two marks of a great man,
including the mark of the invisible crown of the head, with the three bodies fully perfected.
Place this mudrā upon the crown of the head and release it as appropriate.
Next, bind the Lotus Family Samaya Mudrā: join the palms like a lotus bud at the level of the heart.
The dhyāna-wisdom of giving and wisdom stand upright together,
while the remaining six perfections unfold and bend like an eight-petaled lotus flower.
Having formed the mudrā,
one recites the mantra and enters the samādhi of the yoga of profound great compassion,
visualizing the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara filling the entire realm of space.
Together with immeasurable holders of lotuses,
may you grant me your empowerment.
Again, perform this visualization.
From the seal, immeasurable rays of light stream forth,
illuminating and touching the seeds of affliction within the fundamental ālayavijñāna of sentient beings in the six realms of existence,
whereby one attains the great compassion that is impartial toward self and others and free from objective conditions.
One swiftly attains the illusion-like samādhi,
manifests various bodies according to the types of beings within the six realms of existence,
and achieves the four kinds of unhindered liberation.
Possessing sixty-four kinds of Brahma-sounds,
his perfect voice simultaneously responds to all sentient beings as he attains the Way of the Buddha.
The mantra is:
*Namaḥ kṣamārapāṇaye oṃ praṇamāmi nāthāya svāhā*. By means of the empowerment of this seal and mantra, [the following occurs].
One becomes equal to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and shall attain the ten stages, the ten masteries, and the three types of mind-made bodies.
With this mudrā placed upon one's own mouth, it is then released.
Next, bind the Samaya-mudrā of the Vajra Family: with the two hands back-to-back, interlace the thumbs and ring fingers with the middle and little fingers respectively.
Having completed the binding of the mudrā, recite the mantra.
He entered the samādhi of the bodhicitta and beheld the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi and the assembly of immeasurable wrathful deities, including Krodhamuṇḍa, pervading the entire realm of space.
"May you grant me your empowerment.

Then, visualize that immeasurable light streams forth from the mudrā, touching all sentient beings—those in the uncertain destinies, those in the various realms of rebirth as ordinary beings, and those following the two vehicles.
One shall swiftly attain great bodhi.
The mantra is:
*Namaḥ samantavajrāṇām oṃ vajranivārya svāhā*. By reciting this while forming the mudrā and focusing the mind, [the goal is achieved].
Before long, you shall attain the vajra body, speech, and mind of Vajrasattva,
and be able to expound the wheel of the secret teachings,
thereby accomplishing the superior, middling, and inferior siddhis for all sentient beings without exception.
One will swiftly and suddenly realize siddhi.
Thereupon, one should release this mudrā before one's own heart while forming this thought:
In all world-systems without exception,
there are immeasurable and boundless sentient beings who,
although they have resolved upon unsurpassed bodhicitta, [do not yet practice it].
Although they have accumulated the provisions of merit and wisdom,
because they lack the sublime Dharma empowered by the skillful means and wisdom of yoga,
their roots of goodness decline and various māras gain the opportunity to interfere.
How does one introduce them to the wheel of liberation?
For each and every sentient being,
one teaches the subtle Mahāyāna of the three secrets yoga.
One will swiftly and suddenly attain the supreme fruits of both mundane and supramundane siddhi.
By generating such a mind,
one becomes adorned with the armor of the great vow.
Then, form the supreme mudrā of Vajrabhairava:
clench the hands in the inner-binding gesture with the ring and little fingers extended side by side;
bend the index and middle fingers of the right hand like a hook.
The backs of the first joints of the *kṣānti* (patience) and *praṇidhāna* (vow) fingers should be shaped like a three-pronged vajra;
the *dhyāna* and *prajñā* fingers are both extended straight and pressed against the sides of the *kṣānti* and *praṇidhāna* fingers.
The mantra is:
Oṃ vajrābhipretapadāya svāhā. With this mudrā, touch the five locations—the forehead, the left and right shoulders, the heart, and the throat.
Scatter [the flowers] upon the crown of the head.
By forming this mudrā, reciting the mantra, and focusing the mind,
one becomes armored in the vajra mail.
His body is identical to that of Vajrapāṇi, with majestic radiance blazing brilliantly.
He is attended by immeasurable and boundless messengers of the vajra family;
no obstructing difficulties or sentient beings with unwholesome minds can cause him harm.
From the upper reaches of the realm of empty space down to the limit of the wind-circle below,
all those belonging to the classes of sky-faring and earth-dwelling Vināyakas and others shall give rise to a heart of loving-kindness.
For a bodhisattva who is unable to practice the secret words and deeds due to obstacles,
one should next bind the seal of the Bodhisattva Vajracakra and recite the mantra. By doing so,
the one who enters the maṇḍala shall receive the three types of bodhisattva vows that are unobstructed throughout the three periods of time.
By entering the maṇḍala,

one’s body and mind become fully endowed with the samaya and unconditioned prohibitions (*asaṃskṛta-śīla*) numbering as many as the atoms within worlds as numerous as the atoms of ten *paramāṇu-kṣetra* universes.
This applies even to such acts as bending or stretching, looking up or down, speaking or breathing, or the arising of thoughts and mental movements.
If one has forgotten the bodhicitta or regressed from their roots of virtue,
by reciting and contemplating this seal-mudrā and mantra through its sublime skillful means,
one can eliminate transgressions and faults.
The samaya, as before, becomes doubly radiant;
because it can purify body, speech, and mind,
one thereby achieves entry into all mandalas.
Having received the empowerment and the *samaya*,
one should form the mudrā and recite [the mantra] seven times.
Cross the two hands with the palms facing inward.
The powers of exertion extend together;
the straightness of patience and aspiration encircles the initial section of the power of exertion,
with their respective peaks meeting one another.
Holding the meditative concentration (*dhyāna*) and wisdom (*prajñā*) together straight before the heart, recite the mantra:

*Namo siddhividyādhipataye tathāgatāya | Jvala jvala mahākrodha-vajri | Sthātha sthātha sarvaduṣṭān | Trāyitā trāyitā vidhama niḥpātaya trāmaṃti siddhi-giri traṃ svāhā.* While reciting this mantra, perform the following visualization:
May all sentient beings within the three realms, throughout the six destinies, across the entirety of space and the universal dharma-realm,
swiftly enter the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajra Realm and become equal to the Great Bodhisattva Vajrasattva.
Next, one should visualize a wind-wheel beneath one's body.
One visualizes a black syllable *haṃ*, which gradually takes on a shape like a crescent moon;
its dimensions are entirely proportionate to the wind-wheel.
One should contemplate the words of truth,
namely that all phenomena are free from all causes and conditions.
Next, one should visualize the syllable *vaṃ* upon the wind-wheel.
The white light gradually draws forth and becomes complete,
its size equaling that of the original water-circle.
One should contemplate the words of truth,
namely that all phenomena are by nature beyond verbal expression.
Furthermore, one should visualize the syllable *praṃ* upon the wheel of water.
It transforms into a golden tortoise,
emitting golden light that gradually expands to immeasurable yojanas; at that time,
one should contemplate the true meaning.
That is to say, by means of the fact that the ultimate reality (*paramārtha*) of all phenomena is unattainable,
one should further visualize the syllable *kha* within emptiness,
which transforms into the Tathāgata Vairocana.
One should contemplate the true meaning:
that all phenomena are like space,
and the color of the Buddha’s body is like the light of the full moon.
Upon his head he wears a vajra-precious crown;
his body is adorned with necklaces and ornaments;
he is clad in exquisite celestial garments and forms the supreme mudrā of bodhi.
He gave rise to profound compassion,
[seeing that] all sentient beings were being scorched by the fires of the afflictions of greed, hatred, and delusion,
and had accumulated immeasurable, most evil, unwholesome karma.
Visualize the Buddha Vairocana,
from whose entire body flows the nectar-like water of the eight qualities,
its color like that of white jade.
The fire of afflictions of all sentient beings throughout the six realms is drenched [by this rain],
for the golden wheel and the tortoise’s back have become a great ocean of fragrant milk; therefore,
one should bind the *siddhi* of the Ocean Seal (*Sāgaramudrā*).
The ten fingers are bound within, palms facing upward and rotated to the right.
Recite this secret mantra:
Oṃ vimārudani hūṃ. This is for the sake of accomplishing the transformation-lotus.
One should contemplate the syllable-gateway RAṂ,
from which red flames radiate and form a fire-wheel;
its shape is triangular.
The gradual progression is similar to that of a water wheel;
in an instant, a great eight-petaled lotus flower suddenly emerges from the back of the golden tortoise.
The stem is made of vajra,
vast and immeasurable yojanas in extent;
within the flower pedestal, one contemplates the letter-gateway A.
One should contemplate the true meaning:
namely, that all phenomena are fundamentally unarisen,
flowing forth from the dharmadhātu through the gateway of the letter A.
The King of Mountains, Sumeru, emerges leaping forth.
In order to accomplish the Wondrous High Mountain,
one should form the Seal of the Accomplished King of Jewel Mountains.
Interlace the ten fingers within to form a fist;
join them together and extend them upward.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ ajara hūṃ. By means of this mudrā, mantra, and samādhi,
one immediately becomes Mount Sumeru, the king of mountains, composed of the four jewels and surrounded on all sides by seven concentric circles of golden mountains.
Within the mountains there is water possessing the eight meritorious qualities.
From the sides of this king of mountains, four terraces extend outward;
the devas, such as the Four Great Kings, each dwell in their respective directions.
Immeasurable retinues guard the Vajra-Peak Jewel Pavilion.
That mountain is eighty-four thousand yojanas in length and breadth,
and its ground is level and even.
To make [the foundation] firm, dense, and solid like a vajra, reaching down to the limits of space,
one should form the Vajrakīla mudrā:
the fingers of the hand of wisdom enter from between the back of the hand of the vow.
The same applies to the intervals between patience (*kṣānti*), entry (*praveśa*), and the power of aspiration (*praṇidhāna-bala*).
The peaks of aspiration extend outward from the intervals between generosity (*dāna*), ethical discipline (*śīla*), diligence (*vīrya*), and patience.
The remaining perfections (*pāramitā*) each support one another with their respective peaks.
Having formed the mudrā, recite the secret mantra;
visualize it as becoming a vajra-kīla,
emitting immeasurable, fierce flames.
Drive it into the earth with the index finger;
recite once for each drive, stopping after three repetitions.
Thus, a firm boundary of the earth is established.
The mantra is:
Oṃ kili kili vajravajri jñāna bandha bandha hūṃ phaṭ. By means of the empowerment of this mudrā and mantra, [the obstacles are bound].
If one establishes [the practice] within the site of the maṇḍala for recitation without removing all faults and inauspiciousness according to the ritual rules,
various obstacles and difficulties will be summoned.
By virtue of the empowerment of this mudrā, it becomes a vajra-seat;
the celestial Māras and all obstructors shall not cause harm or affliction.
With little exertion of effort, one will swiftly attain great accomplishment.
According to the size of the mind, one should know that the altar site must correspond [to it]. Next, one should bind the seal of the Vajra Wall for the cardinal directions and corners;
this follows the previous stake seal, with the wisdom fingers (jñāna-mudrā) opened and held upright.
The sides are shaped like walls.
One should visualize the mudrā forming a vajra,
from which flow forth immeasurable, blazing vajra flames.
Performing the right-turning mudrā three times around the body,
according to the dimensions of the maṇḍala, it becomes a vajra fortress of adamantine solidity.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ sarā sarā vajraprākāra hūṃ phaṭ. By means of binding the mudrā, reciting this mantra, and performing the mental visualization and empowerment, [the vajra enclosure is established].
Even all the Buddhas do not transgress against it,
let alone other difficult-to-tame beings,
such as the Vināyakas or venomous creatures with sharp fangs and claws, who would be able to invade or oppress it.
Furthermore, the yogin should visualize a great jeweled palace upon the summit of Mount Sumeru.
This palace is composed of priceless mani-jewels;
it is perfectly square and complete with four gates.
To the left and right of its gates stood auspicious banners;
the eaves and railings encircled it,
with strings of pearls and necklaces hanging everywhere.
Bells and tinkling chimes, along with various silk banners,
were interspersed as ornaments, spread throughout the palace;
when stirred by a gentle breeze, they produced harmonious and elegant sounds.
Furthermore, at the four corners outside the palace and at the corners of the various gates,
they were adorned with vajra-jewels in the form of half-moons and full moons.
Rows of jeweled pillars stood there, from which exquisite celestial garments hung down.
Fragrant clouds spread everywhere, raining down a profusion of various flowers.
Furthermore, outside of that, there were rows of immeasurable kalpa-trees,
while the devas vied with one another to play a multitude of exquisite musical instruments.
Having visualized this— jeweled vases with *argha* offerings, celestial exquisite food and drink,
and lamps made of *maṇi* gems— one recites this verse.
By the power of my merit, the power of the Tathāgata’s empowerment,
and the power of the Dharma-realm, I abide in universal offering.
Having spoken this verse, he remained.
Then, one forms the Great Ākāśagarbha Treasury Seal:
perform the vajra-bind with the ten fingers,
and contract the thumbs and forefingers like a jewel.
Extending both meditative concentration (*dhyāna*) and wisdom (*prajñā*) while pressing upon patience (*kṣānti*) and aspiration (*praṇidhāna*),
generosity (*dāna*), wisdom, and ethical discipline (*śīla*) are then united like a banner.
Having formed this mudrā, recite the secret mantra (*mantra*).
Visualize that from the mudrā flow forth the aforementioned offering implements, celestial palaces (*kūṭāgāra*), and so forth. The mantra is:
Oṃ gaganasvabhāva vajra hoḥ. By means of this secret mantra and mudrā, they are consecrated.
Even if one does not succeed in visualizing them,
they all become a truly vast and sublime offering,
for this is established by the very nature of reality (*dharmatā*).

Furthermore, in the center of the jeweled pavilion, one contemplates the syllable A; on both sides, one contemplates the syllable HŪṂ (drawn out). These are the seed-syllables of the dharmakāya of Amṛtakuṇḍalī.
Next, in the eastern direction, one contemplates the short-syllabled HŪṂ.
This is the seed-syllable of the Dharmakāya of Trailokyavijaya.
Furthermore, in the south, one should visualize the syllable TRĀṂ;
this is the seed-syllable of the Dharmakāya of Krodhavajragarbha.
Furthermore, one should visualize the syllable *hṛ* (in the double-syllable form) in the western direction;
this is the seed-syllable of the dharma-body of the youth Vajrasena.
Next, one should visualize the syllable *aḥ* in the northern direction.
This *Vajrakaṇi*— the ancient translation of which is "Vajra Youth"— is the seed-syllable of the Dharma-body (*dharmakāya*).
One should then form the mudrā of the Bodhisattva Vajrakāraṇa in order to bring about the accomplishment of the *ājñācakra-maṇḍala*.
Because it causes all sentient beings to universally and silently enter mandalas such as the Vajradhātu,
the practitioner likewise enters all mandalas.
Because one attains the reception of all empowerments,
all maṇḍalas established according to the activities are accomplished as auspicious,
pure, and neither increasing nor decreasing.
Because all Tathāgatas praise it,
one should bind the Vajra-Cause mudrā and recite the mantra.
Form vajra-fists with both hands.
The powers of progress, generosity, and wisdom are mutually interlocked;
by placing the mudrā upon one's own mouth and reciting [the mantra] three times,
one accomplishes entry into all maṇḍalas, such as the wheel of commands of the Vajradhātu.
Next, place it upon the crown of the head;
this constitutes receiving all empowerments.
Then, press the seal upon the established object or form.
Furthermore, when one contemplates the mandalas of the resultant [state] and so forth,
one truly establishes the wheel-maṇḍala just as Vajrasattva himself did.
One recites this secret mantra, saying:
Oṃ vajracakra hūṃ jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ. Next, bind the seal of the Vajra-jewel chariot (*vajraratna-ratha-mudrā*):
interlace the ten fingers with the palms facing upward.
The *vajra-pāṇi* (forceful) fingers are positioned side-by-side as supports;
with the *dhyāna* and *prajñā* fingers, each presses down upon the base of the *vajra-pāṇi* fingers.
One should visualize the Vajradūta (Vajra Messenger) driving the Vajra-jeweled chariot.
Traveling through the air, he arrived at the world of Abhirati.
He recited the secret mantra three times, saying:
*Oṃ tūru tūru hūṃ*. By virtue of the empowerment of this secret word and mudrā, [he reached his destination].
The seven-jeweled carriage arrived at the great assembly in the World of Supreme Joy of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya,
where they invited the honored deity Amṛtakuṇḍalī Bodhisattva,
along with his retinue of great wrathful bodhisattvas.
Surrounded by immeasurable bodhisattvas making offerings, one mounts this chariot.
Next, form the seal for inviting the chariot:
based on the previous seal, move the *dhyāna* and *prajñā* fingers toward the body while extending the *kṣānti* and *praṇidhāna* fingers.
Recite the secret mantra three times; the mantra is as follows:
*Namo siddhyeṣṭivikāya tathāgatāya oṃ vajragīyanīyakarṣaya svāhā*. By means of the empowerment of this mudrā and mantra, [the rite is accomplished].
The assembly of sages comes from their respective native lands and dwells in mid-air above the site of practice (*bodhimaṇḍa*).
Next, perform the seal for inviting the samaya of the principal deity (*iṣṭadevatā*) to descend upon the site of practice: interlace the ten fingers with the palms facing inward to form fists.
The perfection of meditation enters the palm;
with the perfection of wisdom, beckon it toward the body.
Recite the secret mantra as follows:
Oṃ vajratlekhīye hībhagavan amṛtakuṇḍali svāhā. By means of this mantra and mudrā, it is empowered.
Because the Bodhisattva does not transgress his original vow,
he proceeds immediately to the assembly at the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*).
Next, he should expel all Māras who create obstacles and difficulties.
One should employ the mantra and mudrā of the wrathful eyes of Trailokyavijaya;
upon the pupils of both eyes,
one should visualize the syllable *Hīḥ* transforming into a sun disc.
Immeasurable majestic light flows forth;
upon each path of light,
there are various vajra-flames and fierce, sharp vajra-pestles.
With furrowed brows and wrathful eyes, he looked back toward the assembly of Bodhisattvas;
by this vajra-terrible gaze,
all the māras hidden within the assembly were [overawed].
They all retreated and dispersed. Beholding this,
the principal deity and the assembly of sages were all filled with joy.
Next, form the mudrā of the Vajra Net of the Upper Direction.
This is similar to the previous wall mudrā, except that the thumbs and middle fingers each grasp the lower joints of the ring fingers and little fingers.
Once the mudrā has been formed:
Visualize the mudrā as a vajra.
Furthermore, from the mudrā, immeasurable vajras stream forth;
each vajra emits boundless flames of majestic brilliance.
Forming a continuous net,
rotate the seal three times above the crown of the head.
Recite this secret mantra:
Oṃ viśvapara-ṛkṣa-vajra-pañjara hūṃ phaṭ. By means of the empowerment of this mantra of the Net Seal (Pañjaramudrā), [the following occurs].
This immediately forms a vajra net, firm, solid, and indestructible.
Next, bind the mudrā of the secret seam for the fire enclosure: cover the back of the right hand with the left hand, and extend the *dhyāna* and *jñāna* fingers.
Having completed the mudrā, one should perform this visualization: from the mudrā, blazing vajra flames flow forth.
Recite the mantra three times.
Circumambulate the body three times to the right.
Visualize that outside the vajra wall,
it is surrounded by a circling of flames.
Recite this secret mantra:
Oṃ asama-vajre hūṃ phaṭ. Furthermore, bind the Great Samaya Mudrā: interlace the ten fingers within to form fists.
The *kṣānti* and *vara* [fingers] are extended straight;
the *jyeṣṭha* [finger] is bent like a hook;
and they are positioned on both sides of the *kṣānti* and *vara* [fingers], forming the shape of a three-pronged vajra.
With meditative concentration and wisdom joined to the power of exertion,
perform three clockwise circumambulations with the seal and recite the mantra three times to protect the boundary outside the fire enclosure.
Recite the mantra:
Oṃ śaṅkhamahāsamaya svāhā. By means of the empowerment of this mudrā and mantra, [the purpose is accomplished].
As stated in the *Uṣṇīṣavijaya Sūtra* regarding the Golden Wheel-Turning King and others:
"If there is someone who recites and maintains the Uṣṇīṣarāja and other such *uṣṇīṣa* mantras,
then within five hundred *yojanas*, those who practice the secret mantras of other sections [will be overcome]."
"Please, O Honored One, consider this:
the Noble One neither descends nor grants siddhi."
Because it is encompassed by the majestic power of the One-Syllable Uṣṇīṣa,
if one binds this great boundary (mahā-sīmā),
even those who are nearby and engaged in the recitation of the Uṣṇīṣarāja will [be protected].
They cannot be obstructed;
their power cannot be taken away,
and all other mantra sections they maintain will swiftly attain accomplishment.
Next, form the mudrā for offering the flower seat: join the two hands in the lotus-clasp (*padma-añjali*).
With the thumbs (*tarjanī*) and middle fingers (*madhyamā*), pinch the tips of the ring fingers (*anāmikā*) and little fingers (*kaniṣṭhikā*) respectively to form the pedestal;
the remaining fingers are held like a vajra.
Form the mudrā of contemplation into a vajra-lotus.
Furthermore, visualize that immeasurable vajra-lotus seats flow forth from the mudrā and are offered to the principal deity,
the assembly of noble ones, and so forth.
Recite this secret mantra:
Oṃ vajramaitrāya svāhā. By forming this mudrā and reciting the secret mantra, [the purpose is accomplished].
Once the principal deity and the retinue have each truly taken their seats,
the yogin should prepare two new vessels for the arghya offering.
A conch shell, or one made of gold, silver, various jewels, refined copper,
or even down to clay or wood— filled to the brim with fragrant water and with fresh flowers floating upon it—
one should hold it with both hands at the level of the forehead.
Then one should contemplate the tutelary deity: The body of Cundī is as translucent as emerald beryl;
His majestic radiance surpasses the blazing flames of the kalpa, He wears the sun-disk and displays a frowning brow with a wrathful smile.
With sprouts and buds appearing above and below, his thousand eyes gaze without blinking;
he blazes brilliantly like the sun. His thousand hands each grasp vajra weapons and implements, and upon his head he wears a crown of vajra-jewels.
Adorned with a dragon necklace and a tiger-skin skirt,
surrounded by an immeasurable host of wrathful Vajras and various deities acting as attendants and guardians—
visualizing this clearly, one dwells within the maṇḍala.
Furthermore, one contemplates the argha water flowing forth and showering upon the Principal Deity and the assembly of noble ones; with a single drop of water,
one is able to create an ocean-like cloud of argha that pervades all Buddha-fields.

One should recite the subsequent secret mantra: *Namo ratnatrayāya | namo vajrakrodhāya | oṃ amṛtakuṇḍali hana daha paca bhañja hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*. By offering this *argha* perfumed water, one swiftly attains the pure and wondrous *dharmakāya*.
Next, form the Vajra-unguent mudrā. Consecrate the unguent and offer it to the principal deity and the assembly of noble beings.
As for this mudrā, grasp the right wrist with the left hand.
Extending the right hand, raise the palm five times in the manner of the gesture of fearlessness (*abhaya-mudrā*).
Having formed the seal, recite the secret mantra.
One contemplates that from the seal flows forth clouds and oceans of fragrant ointments,
which pervade all worlds throughout the entirety of space and the dharma-realm,
filling before the assemblies of holy multitudes in the great oceans of buddha-fields as numerous as atoms.
Each person holds an incense box with their own body,
making offerings to each individual honored one to constitute a vast offering.
Recite this secret mantra:
Oṃ ghaṇṭā-maṇi-vajraṇī-pratijñā-hūṃ svāhā. While reciting this mantra, one should form the mudrā and maintain focused attention.
One will swiftly attain the fivefold Dharma-body (pañcadharmakāya) and be able to dispel the burning heat of the afflictions (kleśa) of all sentient beings.
Next, bind the Vajra-flower mudrā and consecrate the flowers to offer them to the Principal Deity and the assembly of noble ones.
Down to a single flower,
all become immeasurable clouds and oceans,
universally making offerings to the entire assembly of holy ones.
If there are no flowers, one should merely form this mudrā as an offering.
As for the mudrā: with the ten fingers of both hands interlaced with the palms facing inward, bend the tips of the index fingers (tarjanīs) into a circle so that their points touch one another.
With meditative concentration and wisdom joined by the power of exertion,
once the mudrā has been formed,
one should recite the secret mantra while further contemplating that various clouds of flowers flow forth from the mudrā like a vast ocean.
Pervading all worlds, the realm of empty space, and the dharma-realm,
they fill the assemblies of great multitudes before the oceans of buddha-fields within every atom, performing vast offerings.
Recite this secret mantra:
Oṃ maṇidhara vajradhara svāhā. By forming this mudrā and reciting the secret mantra with empowerment, [the purpose is accomplished].
One will swiftly attain the thirty-two marks [of a Great Being].
This enables the flower of the bodhicitta to blossom within all sentient beings.
Next, form the Vajra Incense Mudrā; empower the incense and offer it to the Principal Deity and the assembly of noble ones.
Join the backs of the two hands together;
press the sides of the tips of the *tarjanī* fingers against each other;
and with the *śamaya* and *jñāna* fingers, pinch the sides of the *tarjanī* fingers respectively.
Having completed the mudrā, one should immediately perform this visualization:
from the mudrā flows forth a vast ocean of clouds of burning incense,
pervading all worlds throughout the entirety of space and the dharma-realm.
Pervading everywhere with fragrant incense,
they made offerings to the great ocean-like assemblies in all lands as numerous as atoms;
before each and every member of the holy assembly, there appeared their own bodies.
Burn various blended incenses as an offering and recite this secret mantra:
Oṃ dhūma-śikhi-kuruvāriṇi svāhā. By forming this mudrā and reciting the mantra to empower it, [the rite is accomplished].
One will swiftly attain unimpeded wisdom.
Next, bind the Vajra Food and Drink mudrā to offer it to the primary deity and the assembly of noble ones.
Join the two hands in the *padma* (lotus) palm gesture.
Having completed the mudrā, recite the secret mantra.
Furthermore, one should contemplate that from the mudrā there flow forth immeasurable clouds and oceans of food and drink,
pervading all worlds throughout the entire realm of empty space and the dharma-realm.
One accomplishes infinite and vast offerings before each and every holy being within the ocean-like assemblies of Buddhas throughout all atom-sized buddha-fields.
If one empowers even a small amount of worldly food and drink with this seal, [it becomes an offering].
Thus, they become clouds and oceans of celestial ambrosial food,
which are universally offered to all the noble ones.
Recite this secret mantra:
Oṃ malla malla maṅgaliṇi pratīhāri hana vajriṇi svāhā. By binding this mudrā and reciting this secret mantra, [the purpose is accomplished].
Swiftly realize the taste of the three liberations and obtain the food of dharma-joy and the bliss of dhyāna.
Next, form the Vajra Lamp Mudrā to offer to the principal deity and the assembly of noble ones.
This mudrā is formed by making a fist with the right hand and extending the ring finger.
Press the *dhyāna* seal forward as armor.
With the tip of the *dhyāna* peak, pinch the center of the *kṣānti* [seal] and rotate it to the right to illuminate.
Then one performs this visualization: from the seal, there flow forth immeasurable clouds and oceans of vajra lamps,
pervading all worlds throughout the entirety of space and the dharma-realm,
filling before the assemblies of the Buddha’s ocean-like congregations in every atom-sized buddha-field.
This constitutes a vast offering.
By empowering a single lamp with this mudrā,
it immediately becomes an infinite ocean-like cloud of vajra lamps.
One is able to universally make offerings to the ocean-like assemblies of noble ones who illuminate all Buddha-fields.
Recite this secret mantra:
Oṃ jvala-maṇi-nidhi-nyāsa-svāhā. By means of the empowerment of this secret mantra and mudrā, [the purpose is accomplished].
One will swiftly obtain the Tathāgata’s five pure eyes. Next, bind the seal of universal offering (samantapūjā-mudrā) to make offerings to the primary deity and the assembly of noble ones.
Interlace the first joints of the ten fingers of both hands.
Having formed the mudrā,
recite the mantra while contemplating that from the mudrā there flow forth oceans of clouds of various offerings,
such as celestial music, song, dance, and playful delights.
Divine and exquisite garments, food and drink, lamps, *argha* water, auspicious vases, *kalpavṛkṣa* trees, precious banners, flags, canopies, and various other such treasures—
all manner of objects of enjoyment possessed by all gods and humans.
With a multitude of diverse articles for offering—
such as the articles of offering described in the Mahāyāna sūtras—
they pervade all worlds throughout the entirety of space and the dharma-realm, reaching the oceans of Buddha-assemblies within every single atom of all buddha-fields.
Before each member of the assembly of noble ones, there is a genuine offering.
Recite this secret mantra:
*Namo sarvabuddhabodhisattvānāṃ | svāhā khaṃ udagati sphara hīṃ gagana kaṃ svāhā*. Having made the offering:
Clearly visualize the principal deity together with his retinue, and then recite this hymn of praise to extol the immeasurable virtues of the Noble One:
*mahāmāraya caṇḍaya vinyarāja sadhvanandanamogaye namaste vajrapāṇaye*. Having thus praised the principal deity, [proceed].
Thereafter, arrange the seed-syllables and bring yourself into the *samādhi* of the Principal Deity.
With both hands in the vajra-bind mudrā, place them facing upward below the navel.
Close your eyes, clarify the mind, and settle the thoughts in meditative concentration.
Arousing great compassion for all sentient beings,
may all beings swiftly realize the samādhi of their chosen deity,
possessing blazing majesty, longevity, and supernormal powers equal to those of the Noble Ones.
Immediately, one should visualize the syllable Oṃ upon the crown of one's own head,
red in color and possessing great radiance that illuminates the ten directions.
Next, one should contemplate the syllable Ā at the heart.
The color is like white jade or snow, shining both internally and externally like the great lunar disc.
Furthermore, one contemplates the syllable *Miḥ* on the two shoulders;
its color is like a rainbow, illuminating all worlds.
Furthermore, one contemplates the syllable *di* at the navel wheel;
its color is like pure white silk, luminous and glossy,
illuminating all the evil realms throughout boundless worlds.
Next, visualize the syllable HŪṂ at the two thighs;
its color is like gold, and its radiant light touches and illuminates the uninterrupted evil realms.
Next, visualize the syllable PHAḤ placed upon the two shins.
Its color is like a dark cloud; by its illumination and touch, it quickly causes all asuras to awaken to the Right Path.
Next, one contemplates the syllable *Ṭha*, which rests upon the palms of the two feet;
it is white in color and its shape is like a half-moon.
Light radiates forth, illuminating and touching all non-Buddhists,
causing them to abandon the net of false views and take refuge in the Triple Gem by means of this Samādhi of Arrayed Syllables.
Having transformed oneself into the deity, the visualization corresponding to the body of the deity is now explained:
[the deity] has four faces and four arms;
the right hand holds a vajra, and the left hand forms the mudrā of wish-fulfillment.
With both hands forming the *karmamudrā*, his body is adorned with a garland of majestic blazing light; he dwells within a lunar disc,
seated upon a crystal boulder that has the color of a blue lotus,
and faces forward with an expression of compassion.
The second face on the right is wrathful;
the third face on the left displays a broad, laughing countenance;
and the fourth face at the back is slightly angry with its mouth open.
Then, one forms the *karma-mudrā* of the Honored One, with the wisdom-hand (*prajñā-hasta*) pressing upon the armor of the means-hand (*upāya*).
The rest is as for the three-pronged form; the wisdom-hand is likewise.
The right hand presses the left, with the arms crossed.
The mantra is:
Oṃ amṛte hūṃ phaṭ. By empowering oneself with this mantra-seal, one becomes equal to the Honored One Amṛta.
According to one's inclination, visualize [the deity] with four arms,
eight arms, or even two or a thousand arms,
abiding in the samādhi of the yoga of the *iṣṭadevatā*.
It must be even more clearly and distinctly visualized.
Next, form the Mudrā of Vajra-family Mother Maṅmokī: interlace the two hands with palms facing inward;
extend the *kṣānti*, *praṇidhi*, *tarjanī*, *madhyamā*, *anāmikā*, and *aṅguṣṭha* fingers together.
It has the form of a three-pronged vajra.
Having formed the mudrā, one should recite this secret mantra:
*Namo ratnatrayāya | namaḥ śrīvajrapāṇaye mahāyakṣasenāpataye | tadyathā | oṃ kuraṇḍadharī bandha bandha hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*. As before, apply the seal to the five places of one’s own body.
Through the empowerment of the Family Mother’s mudrā,
siddhi will swiftly manifest before one,
and all demonic obstacles will be entirely dispelled.
All those among human beings who possess hostile and unwholesome minds shall be utterly destroyed,
and they shall instead give rise to a mind of great compassion toward the yogin.
If one suddenly sees a bad dream or encounters an inauspicious event,
reciting this one hundred and eight times will cause all such things to dissipate,
and one shall obtain great auspiciousness.
The yogin then visualizes this noble lady seated upon a lotus pedestal before the deity,
adorned with crowns and necklaces in the form of a celestial maiden,
holding a five-pronged vajra in her left hand.
With the right hand in the gesture of granting fearlessness,
one should visualize the seed-syllable of the deity in golden letters flowing forth from the mouth of the Family Mother, together with the secret mantra.
The row possesses radiance;
it enters the mouth of the yogin and coils to the right upon the tongue like a flower garland.
Having performed this contemplative practice,
loosen this mudrā at the crown of the head.
Next, bind the Samaya-mudrā of the Honored One by interlacing the thumbs and wisdom-fingers (tarjanīs) so that they enter the palms.
The two hands are joined at the square of the wrists;
the thumbs press against the space between the middle fingers;
the ring fingers and little fingers are extended side by side.
The *vajra-pāṇi* (left hand) is bent like a hook;
the thumb and ring finger of the *kṣānti-praṇidhāna* (right hand) form the shape of a three-pronged *vajra* behind it,
while the *dhyāna* and *prajñā* fingers are both extended.
Place the thumbs on the back of the hands between the *kṣānti* (forefinger) and *praṇidhāna* (ring finger).
Recite this secret mantra:

*Namo ratnatrayāya | namaḥ śrīvajrakrodhāya | oṃ hulu hulu tiṣṭha tiṣṭha bandha bandha hana hana amṛte hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.* Recite this seven times clearly and distinctly, while visualizing the deity (*devatā*) with perfect clarity.
And because one regards oneself as the primary object of veneration,
by virtue of the empowerment of this mudrā and mantra,
the Noble One will not transgress their original vow and will bestow siddhi.
Then, holding the rosary with both hands like a closed lotus bud,
one should recite the secret mantra of the Bodhisattva Vajravāc seven times to empower it.
The mantra is:
Oṃ vajra-guhya-jñāna-padasamaye hūṃ. By means of this mantra, the rosary is consecrated.
Then, reciting the mantra once, move one bead;
thus, by reciting the mantra one thousand times,
using the thumbs and index fingers of both hands.
Hold the beads with the thumb;
let the other three fingers remain extended and straight.
Guide the beads with the left hand and rotate them with the right hand.
In accordance with the manner of turning the wheel of Dharma,
one should recite [the mantra] one hundred and eight times or one thousand times.
If it does not reach one hundred and eight times, it will not suffice for the required number of recitations for the prayer.
At the time of recitation, the mind should not be interrupted;
one should visualize the body as the deity.
When reciting, one should not produce sound.
Neither too slowly nor too quickly,
continue until the *svāhā* syllable is reached and the rosary is completed.
Once the prescribed number of recitations is finished, take up the rosary again, empower it, and set it down.
Furthermore, bind the samaya-mudrā of the principal deity and recite the mantra seven times;
thereafter, bind the mudrā of the Family Mother and recite it seven times,
visualizing [the light] emerging from one's own mouth.
Then, the secret mantras previously held flow out,
entering the mouths of the Mothers of the Families in lines of golden letters,
together with the number of recitations for the secret mantras of the respective tutelary deities.
Then, entrust the merit to the Mother of the Family (Kulīśvarī),
who shall receive, maintain, and protect it so that it is never lost.
Thereafter, bind the Vajrabandha mudrā.
Entering the samādhi of the essential root of the mantra-syllable wheel of the tutelary deity,
one visualizes the syllable *raṃ* upon the pupils of both eyes,
its color like the flame of a lamp.
Slightly bending the neck and closing the eyes,
one should illuminate and clearly perceive the path of the mind with the eye of mental wisdom.
One should then visualize within the chest the perfectly full lunar disc of bodhicitta.
Holding [the mind] within the present physical vessel,
one perceives it with vivid clarity, free from external distraction and movement;
this is due to the water of wisdom and meditative concentration being limpid and pure.
The moon-reflection of the bodhicitta appears therein;
after concentrating the mind on a single object for a long while,
it immediately manifests upon the sphere of perfect luminosity.
With the mind focused on the "honey" of the words, arrange each syllable in a clockwise sequence.
Recite them mentally three to five times,
then contemplate that the initial syllable *Oṃ* signifies that all phenomena are fundamentally unattainable.
When in accord with the meaning,
the mind takes the principle as its object and does not take the words as its object;
this single path of purity pervades the entire dharma-realm.
One immediately enters the second gate, the letter A;
one contemplates that all phenomena are fundamentally unarisen.
Having contemplated this, one immediately enters the third gate, the syllable *mri*.
In all phenomena, a self is unattainable;
thus, one realizes the equality of the true nature (*tathatā-svabhāva*) and accomplishes merits as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
Next, one should enter the fourth gateway, the letter *Ṭi*.
The suchness of all phenomena is unapprehendable.
Having observed this with discernment,
one perceives within that there exists the subtle meaning of the causal conditions consisting of the subject and object of cognition.
One immediately enters the fifth *huṃ* gateway.
Since all causes—both subject and object—are unapprehendable, and because there is nothing to be apprehended, there is likewise no fruit to be attained.
Next, one enters the sixth *pha* gateway.
The fruit of all phenomena is unattainable.
Because the fruit is non-apprehendable, it constitutes the ultimately perfected Dharmakāya,
which is the locus of all untainted phenomena.
One then contemplates the seventh gateway, the letter *ṭha*.
All phenomena are fundamentally unattainable;
because all phenomena are without contention, all phenomena are fundamentally unattainable.
Because all phenomena are unapprehendable, all phenomena are fundamentally unborn.
Because all phenomena are unborn, a self cannot be apprehended within all phenomena.
Because all phenomena are without self, the suchness of all phenomena cannot be apprehended.
Because the suchness of all phenomena cannot be apprehended, the cause of all phenomena cannot be apprehended.
Because all phenomena have no obtainable cause, the fruit of all phenomena cannot be obtained.
Because the fruit of all phenomena has nothing to be acquired, all phenomena are free from contention.
Because all phenomena are free from contention,
one attains the samādhi of the pure, non-conceptual true nature;
this process continues in an endless cycle.
By virtue of being conjoined with a single thought of pure mind,
one attains unimpeded Prajñāpāramitā;
all karmic retributive obstacles and afflictive obstacles from beginningless time are simultaneously and instantaneously extinguished.
All Buddhas of the ten directions and their respective deities will appear before you;
before long, you shall attain the mundane and supramundane siddhis as you desire.
In this present life, he realizes the first stage, the Stage of Joy;
in the subsequent sixteen great lifetimes, he realizes unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment,
at which point he emerges from meditative concentration.
Join the two hands in the vajra-pañjali mudrā;
direct the mind to visualize the principal deity and the assembly of noble ones,
and extol their virtues with a subtle and melodious tone of praise.
Furthermore, offer the five kinds of offerings by directing the mind as previously described.
Then, present the argha water and petition the assembly of noble ones for the siddhi sought within the heart, saying:
"I pray that the Noble Ones will not transgress their original vows and their great compassionate aspirations."
Bestow upon me siddhi. Then,
with the fire-court secret-sewing mudrā and mantra,
rotate to the left to dissolve all the preceding boundary-marks.
Then, forming the mudrā of the chariot, one visualizes the principal deity and their retinue mounting the chariot.
One extends the fingers of the earth-touching and wish-fulfilling gestures outward to escort the holy assembly back to their original land, the world-realm of Abhirati.
The mantra is as before.
Furthermore, bind the seal of the Mother of the Vajra Family as previously described, cast it outward with the *prajñāpāramitā* [gesture],
and recite this secret mantra:
Oṃ vajra-greṣa greṣa vagvan amṛta-kunāli svabhāvānāṃ punar-āgamanāya svāhā. Furthermore, bind the mudrās of the three families and recite the mantra three times.
Having bound the seal for protecting the body,
pay homage to the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, perform walking meditation as you wish,
and recite Mahāyāna sūtras.
Dedicating this merit to all sentient beings,
may they swiftly attain whatever siddhis they seek in their hearts;
may all beings likewise achieve them quickly.
When the yogin eats, he should empower his five limbs with the mantra and mudrā of the Lord of the Family, and then eat.
When sleeping, he should use the mudrā and mantra of the Mother of the Family.
One should empower the five places of one's own body,
as well as the private parts and other impure areas,
by using the mantra and mudrā of the Vajra-hṛdaya of Aśvakarṇa to empower these five places.
No māras shall find an opportunity against him;
he will swiftly attain accomplishment.
The heart-mantra of Ucchuṣma is as follows:
*Oṃ krodhana hūṃ jaḥ: The Ritual Manual for the Accomplishment of the Recitation and Offerings of the Bodhisattva Amṛtakuṇḍalī*, one fascicle.
